King Charles III will welcome the Sultan of Oman to the UK on Tuesday, as the monarch hosts a traditional state visit at Windsor Castle. Charles and Queen Camilla, joined by Prince William and his wife Catherine, the Prince and Princess of Wales, will entertain Sultan Haitham bin Tarik Al Said at a glittering banquet in the historic royal fortress. Working members of the royal family will be out in force for the grand evening affair in St George’s Hall. The event is the first incoming state visit since the Duke and Duchess of Sussex returned to the UK, but Harry and Meghan, who are not working royals, do not take part in official royal engagements. It also marks Andy Burnham’s first state banquet as prime minister, meaning he will be expected to be decked out in white tie and tails and seated next to key guests and close to the king during the celebration. Charles and Camilla will wait for the Sultan on a special dais in the town centre. On arrival, the monarch, Camilla, William, Kate and the VIP guest will take part in a horse-drawn carriage procession through Windsor to the castle, ahead of the ceremonial welcome and inspection of the Guard of Honour in the quadrangle. The pair met in July, when they discussed attempts to restore freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz, with Burnham expressing gratitude for Oman’s mediation efforts in the region. The sultan last visited the king in the summer of 2025 for tea and a private meeting at Windsor Castle. The last state visit by a sultan of Oman was 44 years ago in 1982, when Queen Elizabeth II hosted the late Sultan Qaboos bin Said, Haitham bin Tarik Al Said’s cousin, at Buckingham Palace.
